arguments.title: Expansion Assist cohort comparison — Q1 vs Jul–Sep 2026
arguments.body:
# Expansion Assist cohort comparison — Q1 vs Jul–Sep 2026

Historical comparison note. Cohorts are kept separate; rates are descriptive account-level proportions (outcome count ÷ actual exposures), not a pooled estimate.

## Q1 2026 evidence lane — interim checkpoint

- **Period:** Q1 2026 evidence review; the available February 10 checkpoint reports on December exposures. It is not a complete Jan–Mar exposure-period closeout.
- **Denominator:** 12 actual December exposures with complete 45-day outcome windows at the checkpoint.
- **Complete-window status:** Complete for these 12 December exposures. January exposures were still immature and explicitly excluded; full-quarter maturity/source certification was not established in this checkpoint.
- **Help-or-options requests:** 4/12 = **33.3%**.
- **Expansions:** 2/12 = **16.7%** within the measured window.
- **Customer Success exclusion:** All 12 included exposures met standing current-state eligibility; none had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. Active Customer Success work suppresses exposure.
- **Randomized comparison:** No randomized control was included in this evidence. The recorded rates describe outcomes among exposed accounts only.

## Jul–Sep 2026

- **Period:** July 1–September 30, 2026 requested exposure period.
- **Denominator:** **Not available in the retained source evidence located for this note.** Do not infer the exposure count from operating limits or other periods.
- **Complete-window status:** **Not verified.** No certified full 45-day-window closeout for this period was available in the retained evidence.
- **Help-or-options requests:** Count and rate **not available**; rate cannot be calculated without a certified denominator and outcome count.
- **Expansions:** Count and rate **not available**; rate cannot be calculated without a certified denominator and outcome count.
- **Customer Success exclusion:** The operating rule suppresses accounts with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. A period-specific certification that no such accounts were exposed was not available in the retained evidence.
- **Randomized comparison:** No period-specific randomized assignment/control record was available in the retained evidence. A causal comparison is therefore **not documented** here; do not treat observed exposed-account rates, if later supplied, as causal absent a valid comparison.

## Interpretation and comparison limits

The Q1 checkpoint’s 4/12 request rate and 2/12 expansion rate are descriptive outcomes in a selected, exposed group—not evidence that Expansion Assist caused either outcome. Without randomized or otherwise credible contemporaneous controls, there is no counterfactual rate to estimate incremental lift; eligibility selection, underlying account readiness, Customer Success activity, and other factors may explain some or all of the observed outcomes. Keep requests separate from expansions, do not combine the periods, and do not rank the Q1 checkpoint against Jul–Sep until the latter’s denominator, mature windows, outcome counts, and Customer Success suppression status are source-certified.

args.title: Expansion Assist cohort comparison — Q1 vs Jul–Sep 2026
args.body:
# Expansion Assist cohort comparison — Q1 vs Jul–Sep 2026

Historical comparison note. Cohorts are kept separate; rates are descriptive account-level proportions (outcome count ÷ actual exposures), not a pooled estimate.

## Q1 2026 evidence lane — interim checkpoint

- **Period:** Q1 2026 evidence review; the available February 10 checkpoint reports on December exposures. It is not a complete Jan–Mar exposure-period closeout.
- **Denominator:** 12 actual December exposures with complete 45-day outcome windows at the checkpoint.
- **Complete-window status:** Complete for these 12 December exposures. January exposures were still immature and explicitly excluded; full-quarter maturity/source certification was not established in this checkpoint.
- **Help-or-options requests:** 4/12 = **33.3%**.
- **Expansions:** 2/12 = **16.7%** within the measured window.
- **Customer Success exclusion:** All 12 included exposures met standing current-state eligibility; none had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. Active Customer Success work suppresses exposure.
- **Randomized comparison:** No randomized control was included in this evidence. The recorded rates describe outcomes among exposed accounts only.

## Jul–Sep 2026

- **Period:** July 1–September 30, 2026 requested exposure period.
- **Denominator:** **Not available in the retained source evidence located for this note.** Do not infer the exposure count from operating limits or other periods.
- **Complete-window status:** **Not verified.** No certified full 45-day-window closeout for this period was available in the retained evidence.
- **Help-or-options requests:** Count and rate **not available**; rate cannot be calculated without a certified denominator and outcome count.
- **Expansions:** Count and rate **not available**; rate cannot be calculated without a certified denominator and outcome count.
- **Customer Success exclusion:** The operating rule suppresses accounts with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. A period-specific certification that no such accounts were exposed was not available in the retained evidence.
- **Randomized comparison:** No period-specific randomized assignment/control record was available in the retained evidence. A causal comparison is therefore **not documented** here; do not treat observed exposed-account rates, if later supplied, as causal absent a valid comparison.

## Interpretation and comparison limits

The Q1 checkpoint’s 4/12 request rate and 2/12 expansion rate are descriptive outcomes in a selected, exposed group—not evidence that Expansion Assist caused either outcome. Without randomized or otherwise credible contemporaneous controls, there is no counterfactual rate to estimate incremental lift; eligibility selection, underlying account readiness, Customer Success activity, and other factors may explain some or all of the observed outcomes. Keep requests separate from expansions, do not combine the periods, and do not rank the Q1 checkpoint against Jul–Sep until the latter’s denominator, mature windows, outcome counts, and Customer Success suppression status are source-certified.
